comments.text: cliff diving's entry, from the shell: the screen off, the hardware's interrupt vector at $FFFE pointed at $109F, RAM everywhere but the I/O ($01 = $35), zero page $08-$FF cleared, the random numbers seeded from the shell's $08FD-$08FE, the music's frequency table, the colour scroll's code written at $E000 ($2ABE), the first set of sprites copied in ($10B3), multicolour, the screen at $4400 with characters at $4800 in VIC bank 1, the border black, CIA 1's timer A stopped, the fire button up, the level not yet chosen ($17 = $FF), the raster interrupt at line 0 through $0314 ($10F2), every player's joystick unknown ($7E-$85 = $FF), and the first player's name in the text row
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's header here ($1000-$1004) while it unpacks; once unpacked, the CLD of cliff diving's start-up

the last byte of the packed file's header the shell's unpacker reads; here, the TXS
the interrupt, through the vector at $FFFE since the KERNAL is switched out: A, X and Y saved, then on through $0314 as the KERNAL would
the main loop: whenever the set of sprites wanted ($29) is not the one in place ($28), copies it in ($10B3); everything else runs in the interrupts
copies sprite set A (0, 1 or 2) to $7000: 14 pages from $A000, 12 from $AE00 or 7 from $BA00 ($10E9, $10EF), the copy loop's addresses written into it; $28 the set now in place

the frame's interrupt, at line 0 the first time and at line $FA after: a raster interrupt is acknowledged; the frame counter ($55-$56); multicolour; $D011 with 24 rows, the vertical fine scroll ($0B) and the screen on or off ($37); the screen buffer in use ($08: $4000 or $4400). With $38 set, the event ends ($0900). Otherwise background black, multicolours light blue and brown, the next interrupt at line $61 ($1254), the indicators' sprites ($22BE); then, unless the last frame's work is still running ($10), interrupts back on and the frame's work: the waves, the pose lists, the four objects drawn, now and then tune 4, the colour scroll ($20 = 2), the state's handler ($11B9 by $0F), the music

interrupts on again while the frame's work runs, so that the raster splits further down still happen

jumps to the state's handler, through $43-$44

the next interrupt at line $FA ($10F2)
$11 at 1: the text row blanked, extended colour mode with multicolour, the background black

the raster interrupt at line $61: the indicators' sprites off; the next interrupt at the water's line ($13 less 2, $1379) when the water is on the screen, otherwise at line $EF ($11CB). the sprites' multicolours white and black, and the game's sprites from zero page

the sea rises and falls: its speed ($7A-$7D) gains its acceleration ($76-$79) and its level ($72-$75, the whole lines in $74-$75) gains its speed; the acceleration turns round when $14, counting down, runs out: 120 frames the first time, then every 240 ($33). With the sea on the screen ($70-$71 past it), $13 is the raster line of its surface. When $14 is 1, in the dive, tune 3

starts tune A, interrupts off while it does: for each voice, the track the tune gives it ($C599, from four times A less four), its data pointer ($B0-$B5) and a wait of one frame ($D1-$D3); a voice whose entry is $FF is left as it is. The processor's flags are kept

silences the music: zeroes $D401-$D440 and the driver's variables $B0-$EF, and starts the pulse width sweep at $04xx ($DB)

plays one frame of music, voice 3 to voice 1: a voice still waiting counts down ($D1); as its wait runs out its gate is let go unless the note is held ($C1), and the frame after, it reads its next commands and note. Then the pulse width sweep ($DC) and the vibrato ($E2)
reads the voice's next byte: $EA is skipped, $FF ends the voice (pointer cleared, gate off), below $C0 a note ($C4C8), otherwise a command from the table at $C536
